headline: High Altitude Access and Backcountry Permits
reservation: While general entry to the National Forest is open, popular alpine basins like Ice Lakes may require day-use permits during peak summer. Lodging in Silverton and Telluride is limited; stay-specific systems should be checked via official municipal or forest service websites for changing seasonal requirements.

days.title: Million Dollar Highway History

stops.name: Animas Forks Ghost Town
stops.detail: Explore the remarkably preserved wooden structures of an 1870s mining camp at 11,200 feet.

stops.name: Molas Pass
stops.detail: Stop for panoramic views of the Weminuche Wilderness and the high-altitude needles of the San Juans.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for mountain passes; conditions vary with weather
days.note: High-altitude acclimation is essential before attempting hikes above 10,000 feet.

days.title: Canyons and Thermal Springs

stops.name: Box Canyon Falls Park
stops.detail: Witness a 285-foot waterfall crashing through a narrow quartzite canyon via established walkways.

stops.name: Ouray Hot Springs
stops.detail: Soak in mineral-rich pools surrounded by towering 'Switzerland of America' peaks.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local exploration; conditions vary
days.note: Hot springs hours are subject to seasonal maintenance and capacity limits.

days.title: Vistas of the Box Canyon

stops.name: Telluride Free Gondola
stops.detail: Ride between Telluride and Mountain Village for aerial views of the canyon and surrounding 14ers.

stops.name: Bridal Veil Falls
stops.detail: View Colorado’s tallest free-falling waterfall located at the head of the Telluride canyon.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours between regional towns; conditions vary
days.note: Gondola service pauses for seasonal maintenance in late spring and late autumn.

intel.title: Pass Readiness
intel.text: Fuel is available in Silverton, Ouray, and Telluride, but there are no services on the Million Dollar Highway. Ensure a full tank before crossing Red Mountain Pass.

intel.title: Trailhead Saturation
intel.text: The Ice Lakes trailhead lot fills before dawn in July and August. Utilize local shuttles where available or arrive very early to secure a legal spot.

intel.title: Canyon Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular service is nonexistent on long stretches of Hwy 550 and in remote basins. Paper maps or downloaded offline data are required for navigation.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: High passes like Ophir or Black Bear are only accessible to specialized 4x4s in summer. Check the CDOT website for snow-related closures on the main highways.

intel.title: Afternoon Storms
intel.text: Lightning is a severe risk above the treeline after 12 PM. Plan to finish all high-elevation hiking before the daily summer monsoon clouds build.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental in Montrose or Durango, purchase high-altitude supplies, and allow for a slow ascent to your base town.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance 4WD is required for backcountry passes; standard SUVs are sufficient for the Million Dollar Highway.
plan.goldenHour: Molas Pass for sunrise over the peaks, noting that dawn light varies by season and snow cover.
